questions.q: What actually determines whether a subnet is "public" or "private" in the cloud?
options: A label the provider assigns randomly when the subnet is created
Whether its route table has a route sending unmatched traffic to an internet gateway
Whether the subnet's CIDR block starts with 10.0
Whether a security group has been attached to it
questions.explain: A public subnet's route table routes 0.0.0.0/0 to an internet gateway. A private subnet has no such route, so nothing inside it can reach the internet directly.

questions.q: What does it mean that a security group is "stateful"?
options: It only applies to traffic between regions
If inbound traffic on a connection is allowed, the matching outbound reply is automatically allowed back out
It must be manually reset after every connection
It stores a permanent log of every packet that passes through it
questions.explain: A stateful security group tracks the connection, so you don't need a separate outbound rule just to let the reply to an allowed inbound request leave.

questions.q: How does a network ACL (NACL) differ from a security group?
options: A NACL is attached to a subnet and is stateless (inbound/outbound rules are independent, and it can explicitly deny), while a security group attaches to a resource and only allows
A NACL can only be used in Azure, never in AWS
A NACL and a security group are functionally identical with no real differences
A NACL only filters traffic between two different cloud providers
questions.explain: NACLs attach at the subnet level, evaluate inbound and outbound rules separately, and can explicitly deny traffic — none of which a security group does.

questions.q: What is Azure's equivalent of an AWS security group?
options: A route table
An internet gateway
A Network Security Group (NSG)
A virtual network peering connection
questions.explain: Azure's Network Security Group (NSG) provides the same stateful, resource-attached firewall concept that an AWS security group does.

questions.q: A database server sits in a subnet whose route table has no route to an internet gateway. What does this achieve?
options: The database automatically gets a faster connection to other subnets
The database is placed in a private subnet, so nothing inside it can reach the internet directly
The database becomes publicly accessible by default
The route table setting has no effect on internet reachability
questions.explain: Without a route to an internet gateway, the subnet is private — exactly where you'd want a database layer that should never be exposed directly to the internet.
